title: Scoring Higher, Answering Worse: Mitigating Reward Hacking in Rubric-Based RL via Protocol-Level Rubrics
abstract: arXiv:2609.38847v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Rubric-based reinforcement learning (Rubric-RL) trains language models where no verifier exists. A judge checks each criterion of a rubric, and the verdicts are aggregated into a reward, most often by a weighted sum. We show that this additive aggregation is the weak point. Under a sum, criteria compensate for one another: a policy that misses the one decision that matters can buy the points back with advice nobody asked for. On clinical consultation, such a policy scores higher and answers worse. Rubric coverage rises while appropriateness on held-out physician criteria falls below the untrained model. The medical criteria are not to blame. Grouped so that they must hold together, the same criteria, unchanged to the word, recover a third of the loss; shorter answers recover almost none. translated_title: 得分更高，回答更差：通过协议级评分准则缓解基于评分准则的强化学习中的奖励破解
translated_abstract: 基于评分准则的强化学习（Rubric-RL）用于在不存在验证器的场景下训练语言模型。评审者检查评分准则中的每一项标准，并将判定结果聚合为奖励，最常用的方式是加权和。我们证明了这种加法聚合正是薄弱环节所在。在求和机制下，各标准之间会相互补偿：一个遗漏了关键决策的策略，可以用没人要求的建议把分数“买”回来。在临床咨询任务中，这样的策略得分更高，回答却更差。评分准则覆盖率上升的同时，模型在留出的医师标准上的恰当性却下降到低于未训练模型的水平。医学标准本身并非问题所在：将这些标准分组使其必须共同成立时，完全相同的、一字未改的标准就能恢复三分之一的性能损失；而更简短的回答则几乎无法恢复任何损失。因此，我们提出协议级评分准则，它保留了各项标准所要求的内容，但改变了它们的聚合方式。它将检查[清单中的项目分组……]（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文揭示了基于评分准则的强化学习中加法聚合会使各标准相互补偿从而导致奖励破解（模型得分更高但回答更差），并提出协议级评分准则，通过将标准分组以强制其共同成立，有效缓解了这一问题。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that additive aggregation in rubric-based RL enables reward hacking through mutual compensation of criteria—policies score higher yet answer worse—and proposes Protocol-level Rubrics (ProRubric), which group criteria so they must hold together, effectively mitigating this problem.
